title.narrative: Climate Resilience & Empowerment: Path to Sustainable Rural Livelihoods in Palestine

description.narrative: The project is implemented by the Land Research Center (LRC) across rural communities in Hebron, Bethlehem, Nablus, and Jenin. It aims to strengthen the climate resilience and livelihoods of Palestinian smallholder farmers and cooperatives through environmentally sustainable and gender-responsive practices. By the end of 2028, farming households and cooperatives will have increased their adaptive capacity to climate change, improved access to productive resources, and adopted agroecological methods that enhance soil, water, and biodiversity conservation. Women and youth will play stronger roles in cooperative governance, production, and advocacy for environmental and land rights. Key results include: (1) improved technical and institutional capacity of cooperatives and farmers; (2) diversified and climate-resilient production systems; and (3) increased community awareness and policy engagement on climate justice and sustainable land management. Main activities include capacity building on agroecology and climate-smart agriculture, establishing pilot demonstration farms, developing sustainable irrigation and water harvesting systems, supporting cooperative management and marketing, and engaging in advocacy to influence national environmental and agricultural policies. The project operates within the We Effect CSO Programme Together for Food Security in Palestine (2025-2028), contributing to a rights-based, inclusive, and climate-resilient rural economy.
